parties:
Azam Reza   ------ Accused-Petitioner
 vs
State   ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment: 7. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the petition, the first information report and charge-sheet and other Annexures annexed to the petition. On perusal of those we find that the inquest report has been corroborated by the post mortem report, both reports support the allegation made in the first information report. We further found from the post mortem report that the cause of death is due to shock and injuries mentioned in the report which are anti-mortem, homicidal in nature. Moreover, the deceased was killed in her husband's house and naturally, on that moment, the husband was the best custodian and he is supposed to know the cause of death of the deceased, but the story narrated in the UD Case which was ended in the final report creates presumption about the implication of petitioner in the occurrence. Moreover, we do not find any cause to consider the prayer for bail of the petitioner in the light of the decision referred by Mr Malek, the learned Advocate of the petitioner which was given in an appeal. In such circumstances we do not find any reason to enlarge the petitioner on bail during the pendency of the trial.
